decision_1_governance_mirroring.problem: The owner-decision records that govern this project live in workspace/orchestrator/verified-java-websocket-port-claude/protected/, outside the code repository. Deleting or editing one fails NO branch check when VJWP_PROTECTED_STORE is unset. The governance layer is unbound by anything in the repo, so the artifacts that authorize the work are the least protected things in it.
decision_1_governance_mirroring.decision_detail: Commit a manifest of each decision record's sha256 into the repo. Deleting or editing a governance record must then fail a check. The record CONTENTS stay out of the repository.
decision_1_governance_mirroring.rationale: repos/public/verified-java-websocket-port-claude is a PUBLIC repository. The decision records contain internal deliberation, cost figures, owner reasoning and infrastructure identifiers; committing them publishes all of that permanently. A digest manifest gets the tamper-detection without the disclosure.
implementation_notes: The manifest must be verified by something that RUNS -- a rule that lives only in a _test.go file was finding 3 of this very review and does not count as a gate.

A missing protected store must not silently pass. Absence of the store is different from a matching digest, and the check must distinguish them rather than skipping when VJWP_PROTECTED_STORE is unset -- that is the exact shape of the defect being closed.
Prove the gate by execution before claiming it works: delete a record and read the failure, edit one and read the failure, then restore and read the pass.

decision_2_record_schema_bump.problem: The ledger-integrity lane made supersession machine-visible (a Supersedes field producing a canonical SUPERSEDES token in the hashed rationale, plus evidence/java/ledger-supersessions.json and AuthoritativeSequences). But internal/lab's readiness gate reads the FROZEN record vocabulary and cannot see supersession, so a withdrawn record still reads as authoritative to the one consumer that decides release readiness.
options_offered: Bump to 1.1.0 and teach the gate (recommended)
Decide after the remaining reviews land
decision_2_record_schema_bump.decision: BUMP THE RECORD SCHEMA TO 1.1.0 AND TEACH THE READINESS GATE ABOUT SUPERSESSION.
decision_2_record_schema_bump.rationale: Leaving it deferred means the single consumer that decides release-readiness is reading records the rest of the system considers withdrawn -- which is precisely the failure the supersede mechanism was built to prevent. A supersede mechanism invisible to the gate that matters is not a mechanism.
implementation_notes: Prove the gap first: make a record superseded, run the readiness gate, and read it treating the withdrawn record as authoritative. Then fix, then read the refusal.
The bump must not disturb the frozen prefix. Sequence 35 digests to 3fcd461c... and is now pinned by VerifyFrozenPrefix; verify that pin still holds after the migration.

standing_rule_derived_this_phase.problem: THREE lanes have now escalated the same shape: prose inside an owner-decision-linked artifact goes stale as code moves, and the lane correctly refuses to rewrite it on its own authority. Instances: commit 77d8c23 plus ledger record 36 asserting ws-core byte-identity; commit 85366c4's message claiming work landed 'before any Rust source'; and internal/deltaledger/definitions_layer_split.go:102 naming rust/ws-testee/src/io_loop.rs as the C6 violation_close_frame site when that symbol has lived in ws-driver since the layer split.
standing_rule_derived_this_phase.rule: The freeze boundary already answers this. The owner ruling freezes the ledger prefix THROUGH SEQUENCE 35 and expressly requires the rest to be rebuilt. Therefore: a stale statement in a record at sequence 36 or later may be corrected IN PLACE, because those are this project's own appends and rebuilding them is required, not merely permitted. A stale statement at sequence 35 or earlier requires a NEW SUPERSEDING record and must never be rewritten. A stale statement in a COMMIT MESSAGE is never rewritten -- history stands and a later commit becomes the correction of record.
standing_rule_derived_this_phase.applies_to_the_open_instance: definitions_layer_split.go:102 -- determine the record's sequence, then apply the rule above. Do not escalate this class again unless the record falls at or below sequence 35, or the correction would change a decision rather than a description.
standing_rule_derived_this_phase.caveat: In-place correction is sanctioned for DESCRIPTIONS that have gone stale. It is NOT sanctioned for changing what a record decided or concluded. If a correction would alter the substance of a ruling rather than its description of where code lives, escalate regardless of sequence.
